findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default rather than protected automatically.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block / no ACL restriction
findings.description: No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined, leaving the bucket to potentially inherit permissive defaults and no explicit guard against public exposure.
The bucket stores exported ledger data with acl=private but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial export data unencrypted at rest.
Despite having versioning and logging configured, this bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving model artifacts unencrypted at rest.
Operational runbooks, which may contain sensitive operational details, are stored without any server-side encryption configuration.

The bucket uses the canned ACL 'log-delivery-write', which grants write and read-ACP permissions to the S3 log delivery group; combined with force_destroy this increases risk of unauthorized log tampering or deletion if not tightly scoped.
force_destroy=true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without recourse, removing a safeguard against accidental or malicious data loss for archived reports.
force_destroy=true permits irreversible deletion of financial ledger export data along with the bucket, which is risky for data that likely has compliance/retention requirements.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data uploaded without encryption enforcement
findings.description: A vendor roster file (potentially containing PII/business-sensitive data) is uploaded to a bucket that has no encryption configuration, and the object resource itself does not specify server_side_encryption, so the data is stored in plaintext.
